texts: The incorrect statement is that the damage occurs on the epicardial surface: endocarditis starts on the inner, endothelial surface of the heart: A.
First the endothelium is damaged, one of the white tiles knocked off the inside of a valve door.
Platelets and fibrin, the white plates and red threads, pile onto the bare spot as a sterile thrombus.
A transient bacteraemia, the green germs passing in the river, seeds the thrombus, and the organisms multiply there into a vegetation, the cards sprouting broccoli.
Memory hook: a tile falls off inside, plates and threads pile up, passing germs settle and grow; scrubbing the outside wall does nothing.
